summary: Compose bounded Topo coloring and publish unresolved contacts safely on persistent device buffers.
regressions: Live Rust fixtures exercise sparse, grouped, split-hub, dense exhausted and conflicting seeded graphs in both determinism modes.
Shared source regressions from change 0023 cover palette and iteration bounds; isolated exhausted-mask cases require zero instead of sentinel 64.
Final color and flag agreement, conflict safety, guards, convergence claims and component survivors are independently checked.

Sparse graph fixture components have at most seven contacts; eight rounds cover a worst-case winner per round plus convergence. Four rounds experimentally exhausted the Metal budget and were not certified as complete.
Repeated CPU stages compile each identical source/ABI once per program, but retain every physical-buffer mapping and iteration count; an actual C++ execution regression checks both.
differences: Rust behavior was fixed separately in change 0023. This port mirrors the palette sentinel handling and finalization dispatch.

Generated step/fix kernels test the device convergence grid under a statically bounded launch; a zero grid becomes a no-op. This preserves phase behavior but still incurs dispatch overhead compared with native indirect dispatch.

Nondeterministic whole-loop results may differ in color choices and convergence timing; deterministic outputs remain bit-exact. Dense graphs may leave color-zero contacts for the existing unsolved storage bucket, which still needs production integration.
Native stages preserve original storage with dispatch boundaries and no CPU graph or physics fallback. Vendor compilation and Ascend execution remain unavailable.
Repeated immutable PrimFunc objects reuse source lowering within one program; generated source and per-stage ABI receipts remain present for every dispatch.

Clarification of change 0023: unresolved contacts are retained in the last bucket for warmstart but the existing Rust solver does not solve that bucket. Finalization fixes conflicting solved batches; it does not add a fallback solver or certify every dense-graph contact as solved.
